target.projectDescription: Open-source home-automation server: an asyncio application (homeassistant/) that exposes an HTTP REST API + WebSocket API + webhooks on a self-built aiohttp application stack (components/http, HomeAssistantView), runs 1178 component integrations (device connectors, cameras, media players, cloud assistants, notifier services), dispatches user-defined automations/scripts/services, and pulls data from hundreds of remote vendor APIs. Attacker-relevant input surfaces: unauthenticated webhook HTTP requests (/api/webhook/{webhook_id}), authenticated REST/WebSocket API requests and service calls (service data can carry URLs, e.g. downloader download_file), config-flow UI input, MQTT/device message payloads, YAML configuration, templates, environment variables. Outbound network access is issued through a shared aiohttp ClientSession funnel (helpers/aiohttp_client.py), a shared httpx AsyncClient funnel (helpers/httpx_client.py), direct requests/httpx/aiohttp calls in components.

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: Attackers face (1) unauthenticated HTTP: webhook endpoints /api/webhook/{webhook_id} (WebhookView requires_auth=False; local_only webhooks additionally reject remote senders via network.is_local); (2) authenticated HTTP/REST views (~196 HomeAssistantView references, 104 handler methods of the form 'async def get/post/... (self, request)'); (3) the WebSocket API (513 @websocket_api.websocket_command-decorated handlers + 299 async_register_command sites; message dict msg[...]); (4) service calls through REST/WebSocket/scripts/automations (hass.services.async_register, 265+ registrations; handler reads call.data/service.data, 443 sites; service data can carry URLs, e.g. downloader 'url'); (5) config flows (285 async_step_*(self, user_input) functions; UI form input; e.g. generic camera / octoprint URL fields); (6) device/message buses (MQTT subscription callbacks msg.payload, ~122 sites; doorbell/kodi/etc. events); (7) YAML configuration files and blueprints (load_yaml/yaml.safe_load/parse_yaml); (8) templates (93 .async_render/.render sites; rest_command renders the request URL from service.data variables); (9) environment variables (9 os.environ/os.getenv sites, e.g. SUPERVISOR_TOKEN). Outbound requests go through the shared aiohttp/httpx client funnels, requests.* calls, and direct session method calls (session.get/post/request/ws_connect).

Per operator rule only APIs proven present are emitted; urllib is recorded here as a coverage gap note, not as a query family.

sanitizerObservations: webhook local_only + network.is_local check (components/webhook/__init__.py:144-166): local_only webhooks reject non-local senders outright; webhooks without an explicit local_only value log a deprecation warning and still accept remote senders (flag day 2023.11 per the comment) - a network-origin restriction on the webhook source, not a URL/host restriction on outbound requests
HTTP view authentication (view.py:135 requires_auth gate; components/http/auth.py token validation; ban.py rate limiting) and WebSocket auth phase bound the authenticated source families

voluptuous cv.url validation on URL-typed service/flow/websocket fields (downloader/__init__.py:33, blueprint/websocket_api.py:65, rest/schema.py:53, adguard/__init__.py:35) - URL-shape validation only, no scheme/host allow-listing, so it does not neutralize SSRF to arbitrary hosts

blueprint importer host restrictions: _get_community_post_import_url / _get_github_import_url / gist startswith('https://...') checks (blueprint/importer.py:151/:176/:187) confine fetch targets to the community forum / GitHub api hosts
rest_command/rest/generic-camera/mjpeg URLs come from YAML configuration or config flows (admin-supplied); fixed vendor endpoints (buienradar, duckdns, tado, citybikes, bluesound...) are constants
inputBoundaryInventory.nonVulnerabilityNote: Most fetched URLs are either admin-supplied configuration (rest sensor/command, generic camera, feedreader), fixed vendor API endpoints, or OAuth/refresh flows. The webhook surface is unauthenticated but webhook handlers mostly parse payloads rather than fetch URLs; REST/WebSocket/service boundaries require an authenticated user. These are recorded as candidates only; the extraction deliberately does not presume exploitability of any site (admin-configured URLs are the documented SSRF FP class in WORKFLOW.md 5.3.2 and are expected to be filtered at labeling/report time, not here).

extraction.executionPlan: codeql query compile / codeql query run followed by codeql bqrs decode --format=csv, run sequentially one at a time against core-db; NOT database analyze / SARIF. Per operator instruction, execution is deferred to a later step - this step generates the queries only.
extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries carrying @name/@description/@id/@tags only; intentionally no @kind problem (wrong shape for multi-column candidate tables) and no @kind table (not assumed to exist). Raw BQRS output is decoded directly to CSV.
columnContract: node (location-backed AST node; decodes as file:line:col)
arg_index (0-based positional argument index, -1 when not applicable)
line (1-based start line via Location API; AstNode.getLocation().getStartLine())
match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs (API::moduleImport(...).getMember(...).getACall()); alias-aware for import/from-import idioms of requests/aiohttp/httpx/yarl and the homeassistant.helpers client funnels. Note: moduleImport() forbids dotted names, so the internal funnels are addressed as API::moduleImport("homeassistant").getMember("helpers").getMember("aiohttp_client"|"httpx_client").getMember(...)
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, receiver naming, in-file provenance); catches session variables obtained from the internal funnels, getattr dynamic dispatch and shapes API graphs miss; subject to name-collision noise (e.g. sqlalchemy sessions named 'session' with .get())

extraction.pathFilter: rows are excluded when the node's absolute file path is under tests/ (forward or backslash separators), the file base name matches test_% or conftest.py, or the path contains core-db (the nested CodeQL database directory)
exclusions: tests/ tree (present in the DB; identified by path filter at query time)
core-db/ nested database directory and non-python analysis artifacts are neither scanned nor part of the DB

config-entry data reads (entry.data, 3391 sites) are NOT extracted: config-entry values originate from admin config flows (persisted user input) and are the documented admin-configured-URL FP class; they are modeled, if needed, in Phase 2 as a MySummaries step rather than as extraction rows
entity-state reads (hass.states) and generic hass.data lookups are not extracted (over-broad, weak attacker control)
msg["type"] / msg["id"] websocket routing-key subscripts are filtered out (dispatch metadata, not payload)
network response reads (resp.json()/resp.text()/resp.read()) are not extracted on the source side (response bodies are outputs of SSRF, not its input)

uncoveredCases: Hassio ingress URL composition is f-string based (ingress.py:127-128 url = self._create_url(token, path) + '?' + request.query_string; _create_url interpolates the incoming path): f-strings are not extracted as rows; the outgoing request is captured by the session_arg row at ingress.py:159 and the wrapper row for _handle_request

rest_command/rest switch dynamic dispatch 'getattr(websession, method)(...)' (rest_command/__init__.py:121, rest/switch.py:206) is captured by a dedicated getattr_dispatch family, but only when the getattr first argument is a session-named expression or a client-getter call; other dynamically-dispatched fetches would be missed

Session variables whose assignment provenance crosses files (self._websession assigned in __init__ of the same file is covered by the name-substring rule since the terminal name contains 'session'; cross-file assignment chains are not tracked)

sqlalchemy DB sessions named 'session' collide with the session_arg family (session.get(Entity, pk) in recorder-persisting components); these appear as ast rows and are left for LLM labeling to discard

template-rendered URLs: the template_render source family captures render call sites (e.g. rest_command __init__.py:103) but the variable flow (entity state -> rendered URL) is a Phase 2 MySummaries modeling concern

'from requests import Session' constructor sites are resolved only through API graphs (bare Session() ast matching was intentionally skipped to avoid collisions with locally-defined Session/Client classes)

urllib.request.urlopen / urlretrieve have zero call sites in the tree and are not emitted as query families (operator rule: only APIs proven present); if a future/hidden dynamic urllib use exists it is a coverage gap
msg/msg.get keys that are non-literal (variables) are not extracted; websocket payload reads through destructuring are not covered
Nested-function closure reads are handled through the scope-chain parameter check, but comprehension scopes are not Functions; reads inside comprehensions of outer call/msg parameters may be missed

WebhookView handler aliasing ('get = _handle' class attributes, webhook/__init__.py:212-215) relies on '_handle' being in the handler verb set; views using other custom method names bound to route verbs would need the class-level url/name evidence (not extracted)
The aiohttp web framework is not covered by an augur framework reference (none exists); source/sink shapes are derived from repo evidence only
No rows are filtered beyond the test/core-db path filter; FP-prone families (sqlalchemy sessions, generic .render calls) are retained for labeling with their receiver/module hints

constraintsHonored.notes: No PyVul vulnerability ground truth was consulted: ssrf_sinks.csv, ssrf_sinks.json, ssrf_vulnerability_report.md, ssrf_cost_estimation.md and ast_matcher_failure_analysis.md (all present in the core_vuln tree as untracked analysis artifacts) were NOT opened during this step; only directory listings and git HEAD metadata were inspected to confirm the DB snapshot. Candidate families are derived from repository evidence and the loaded language/pattern references only. Project source, database, and Augur installation files were not modified. Only the three files under iris_manual/SSRF/core/iris were written (exploration/detection.json, extraction/sources.ql, extraction/sinks.ql). No CodeQL query was executed and no LLM labeling was performed, per operator instruction. Historical compile pitfalls honored: no 'module' variable name (moduleHint used), no AstNode.getFile() (Location API used), no unbound this / parentless QL classes, no API::Node <-> DataFlow::Node assignment, binding-safe constant-first predicate bodies, no {{...}} placeholders left, queries target the local CLI 2.25.1 + codeql/python-all 7.x API surface verified in the pack cache.
